title: Insert & query across relationships
summary: Write rows that respect FKs, then JOIN / include to read graphs.

example.sql: SELECT m.title, p.name FROM lab_magazines m JOIN lab_publishers p ON p.id = m.publisher_id;

exercise.prompt: Insert 2 publishers and 3 magazines, commit, then SELECT magazine titles JOINed with publisher names and print them.
exercise.hint: session.commit() makes the rows visible to everyone else; select(...).join(LabL10Magazine.publisher).

from sqlalchemy import String, Integer, Numeric, Boolean, ForeignKey, UniqueConstraint, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class LabL10Publisher(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l10_publishers"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(120))
    magazines: Mapped[list["LabL10Magazine"]] = relationship(back_populates="publisher")


class LabL10Magazine(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l10_magazines"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    publisher_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("lab_l10_publishers.id"))
    publisher: Mapped[LabL10Publisher] = relationship(back_populates="magazines")

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

exercise.solution:
from sqlalchemy import String, Integer, Numeric, Boolean, ForeignKey, UniqueConstraint, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class LabL10Publisher(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l10_publishers"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(120))
    magazines: Mapped[list["LabL10Magazine"]] = relationship(back_populates="publisher")


class LabL10Magazine(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l10_magazines"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200))
    publisher_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("lab_l10_publishers.id"))
    publisher: Mapped[LabL10Publisher] = relationship(back_populates="magazines")

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

with Session(engine) as session:
    acme = LabL10Publisher(name="Acme")
    globex = LabL10Publisher(name="Globex")
    session.add_all([
        LabL10Magazine(title="Monthly Review", publisher=acme),
        LabL10Magazine(title="Data Weekly", publisher=acme),
        LabL10Magazine(title="Outdoor Life", publisher=globex),
    ])
    session.commit()

    stmt = select(LabL10Magazine.title, LabL10Publisher.name).join(LabL10Magazine.publisher).order_by(LabL10Magazine.title)
    for title, publisher in session.execute(stmt):
        print(f"{title} | {publisher}")

body:
Write rows that respect FKs, then JOIN / include to read graphs.

Why it matters: Schema without queries is incomplete. Inserts must satisfy FKs; reads use JOINs (or ORM include) to reassemble the relationship graph you modeled.

SQL ↔ ORM: SQL JOIN ↔ SQLAlchemy selectinload/joinedload ↔ Prisma include/select.
why: Schema without queries is incomplete. Inserts must satisfy FKs; reads use JOINs (or ORM include) to reassemble the relationship graph you modeled.
objectives: Insert parent before child when FKs are required.
Read across a relationship with JOIN or ORM navigation.
pitfalls: Selecting only one table and wondering where related fields went.
mappingNotes: SQL JOIN ↔ SQLAlchemy selectinload/joinedload ↔ Prisma include/select.
teachAlong: Cause: data is normalized across tables.
Effect: JOIN/include reconstitutes the object graph.
Validate: row counts and FK values match your intent.
